podcast.title: Huge Influence on Soul Music
podcast.body: Billy Ward and The Dominoes were a massive influence on the development of soul music. Their lead singers, Clyde McFatter and Jackie Wilson, sang in a style heavily indebted to the church music that the Isley Brothers had also performed, making them a natural inspiration for the Isley Brothers' transition from gospel to doo-wop. "Billy Ward and the Dominoes were a huge influence on the music that became soal, with hit records like Have Mercy Baby."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Paving the Way for Vocal Group R&B
podcast.body: Billy Ward and the Dominoes, particularly with Clyde McPhatter as their lead singer, played a pivotal role in the development of vocal group R&B as a genre. Their records set a precedent that groups like The Famous Flames would pattern themselves after. "Billy Ward and the Dominoes, whose records with Clyde McFatter as lead singer, had paved the way for vocal group R&B as a genre"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Reference Point for Art Rupe's Criticism
podcast.body: Art Rupe critically compared the white backing vocals on Sam Cooke's secular recordings to the sound of Billy Ward and his Dominoes, believing the arrangement was attempting to emulate their style "at best." "They were, in Rube's view, trying to make Sam Cooke sound like Billy Ward and his dominoes at best, and like a symphony orchestra at worst."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

xref.title: Coining the Term "Rock and Roll"
xref.body: Freed famously started referring to the music he played on his radio show as "Rock and Roll." This change in terminology occurred after a New York street musician, who claimed prior usage of the name "Moondog," threatened legal action. One theory suggests Freed derived the term from the 1951 recording "60 Minute Man" by Billy Ward and the Dominoes, which included the lyric "I rock them, roll them all night long," known as African American slang for sexual intercourse, a meaning Freed was likely aware of. "Fried also famously eventually started calling the music he played on his radio show, Rock and Roll."
